identity.title: ALMA Resolves the Molecular Gas in a Young Low-metallicity Starburst Galaxy at z = 1.7

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array observations of CO lines and dust continuum emission of the source RCSGA 032727–132609, a young $z=1.7$ low-metallicity starburst galaxy.

evidence.quote: At the redshift for RCS0327 of $z = 1.7037455 \pm 0.000005$ (cite: Wuyts2014)
At the redshift for RCS0327 of $z = 1.7037455 \pm 0.000005$ (cite: Wuyts2014)

question.value: How are molecular gas, dust and CO excitation distributed in the lensed low-metallicity starburst RCS0327 at z=1.7 once the arc is reconstructed in the source plane?

evidence.quote: In this letter we present the CO and continuum emission of the second-brightest optical giant arc discovered to date, the arc RCSGA 032727–132609 (hereafter RCS0327)
The target RCS0327 was observed as part of the ALMA project 2015.1.00920.S

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: two overlapping SPWs on the line and two for continuum in each observation

evidence.quote: In each observation, two overlapping spectral windows (SPWs) were placed to detect the line and two were placed to detect continuum.
the lines are centered at 127.895 GHz for CO(3-2), 255.746 GHz for CO(6-5)
the lines are centered at 127.895 GHz for CO(3-2), 255.746 GHz for CO(6-5)
Both emission lines were observed using the array configuration C36-1.

evidence.quote: The data for CO(3-2) was imaged using natural weighting returning a synthesized beam size of 2.54$''$$\times$1.85$''$
The observations of the lines CO(6-5) and CO(3-2) were carried out during January 1st and 10th 2016.

method.value: ALMA scripts, clean with natural weighting, taper for CO(6-5), 20 km/s cubes, uvcontsub

evidence.quote: Data cubes using a spectral resolution of 20 km s$^{-1}$ were created for each of the emission lines.

method.value: Extract spectra at e1, e2, u1+u2 and integrate over 127.874–127.976 GHz

evidence.quote: We find that the region going from 127.874–127.976 GHz ($\approx239.3$ km s$^{-1}$) provides a good range for the total emission of the line.

method.value: Fit uv-plane visibilities with a 2D elliptical Gaussian source model through a fixed lens deflection field

evidence.quote: The galaxy emission is fitted assuming a 2D elliptical Gaussian (special case of a Sérsic profile with $n=0.5$) while the lensing potential is fitted by a singular isothermal ellipsoid (SIE).

key_parameters.value: One Gaussian for each CO line; two Gaussians for 450 µm continuum

evidence.quote: we needed two Gaussians in the source plane, since a single component was not enough to account for the whole observed flux outside the PB
supporting the usage of a simple 2d elliptical Gaussian function for the source model

fitting.value: uvmcmcfit MCMC; sampler and priors not stated

evidence.quote: we used `uvmcmcfit`,[^1] which is a `Python` implementation to fit emission models to interferometric data in the $uv$ plane

validation.value: Residual maps from subtracting model visibilities

evidence.quote: In all cases the best fit models appear to account for most of the observed emission.

method.value: L'CO(1-0)=L'CO(3-2)/0.66; H2 mass with alpha_CO=0.8; divide by area from effective radius; SFR over area

evidence.quote: Assuming a CO excitation level valid for SMGs of $L'_{\rm CO(3-2)}/L'_{\rm CO(1-0)}=0.66$ (cite: Carilli_Walter2013)
Because of RCS0327 being cataloged as a starburst, to estimate the molecular mass we will use the values estimated for SMGs and starbursts at high redshift.

method.value: 0.25" source-plane regions; 50 reconstructions from fitting iterations for significance; noise map propagated for 2σ upper limits

evidence.quote: We use a set of 50 source plane reconstructions taken from the fitting iterations to estimate the significance of the detection in each region.
casa (cite: Mcmullin2007) version 4.5.1

used_for.value: uv-plane source-plane reconstruction (modified to use fixed lens deflection field)

evidence.quote: We modified `uvmcmcfit` so that it uses a user provided lensing model deflection field

findings_qualitative.value: CO and dust lie on the star-forming clumps, with dust extending to regions faint in CO(3-2)

evidence.quote: The continuum dust emission follows a similar angular extension and distribution as the molecular gas but also extending towards parts of the galaxy not as bright in CO(3-2), showing a clear spatial offset.

claims.hypothesis: Is RCS0327 a starburst relative to local spirals at similar gas density?
claims.experiment: Compared Sigma_SFR and Sigma_H2 with literature relations
claims.result: Falls above the Daddi2010 relation with alpha_CO=0.8
claims.finding: Supports a merger-driven starburst; position depends strongly on alpha_CO

evidence.quote: We notice that RCS0327 falls above the relation found by (cite: Daddi2010) for MS and starburst galaxies (blue dashed-lines), supporting the starburst nature of RCS0327.

claims.hypothesis: Is RCS0327 similar to local BCDs?
claims.experiment: Compared its properties with BCDs and used the alpha_CO–metallicity relation
claims.result: alpha_CO~25 would put it near the MS with depletion time ~1 Gyr
claims.finding: Low-density starburst similar to BCDs, though conclusions are alpha_CO dependent

evidence.quote: For our estimate of the molecular mass we see that RCS0327 properties are similar to the local BCDs

claims.hypothesis: What is the CO excitation level and does it vary spatially?
claims.experiment: CO(6-5)/CO(3-2) ratios globally and in source-plane regions
claims.result: 1.1±0.2 overall; <0.3 in region 10 to 3.0±0.9 in region 9
claims.finding: Peak at J~5, with higher excitation in clumps

evidence.quote: The ratios go from $S_{\rm CO(6-5)}/S_{\rm CO(3-2)}<0.3$ in region 10 to $S_{\rm CO(6-5)}/S_{\rm CO(3-2)}=3.0\pm0.9$ in region 9.

why_this_method.value: uv-plane fitting retains the maximum information from the data

evidence.quote: Exploring the emission in the $uv$ plane should return the maximum amount of information from the observations

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Fitting the lens and source together from ALMA alone was rejected because the HST model is better

evidence.quote: outperforms in complexity and quality to the model we could find by fitting the lensing potential and source structure together using only the ALMA observations

limitations_admitted.value: Coarse resolution; results depend strongly on alpha_CO

evidence.quote: Our coarse observations already show that RCS0327 is not well described by a single mode star-forming galaxy

referee_caveats_inferred: Gas mass depends on an assumed alpha_CO and r31 spanning 0.8 to 25
Single Gaussian source model with fixed lens model; lens uncertainties not propagated
The SFR upper limit mixes sources of differing definition
